html:
Shiva is one of the great gods of Hinduism, known as Mahadeva, "the great god". With Brahma and Vishnu he forms the three gods of creation, preservation and destruction, but to his own followers, in Shaivism, he is the supreme being who does all three.

He grew partly from the storm god Rudra of the Rigveda. He is shown as an ascetic with matted hair, a third eye, a snake and a trident, living on Mount Kailash with his wife Parvati and their sons Ganesha and Skanda, and riding the bull Nandi. He is also Nataraja, lord of the dance, whose dance creates and destroys the world. In temples he is usually worshipped as the linga, a smooth upright stone.

Kings from India to Southeast Asia built great temples to him:

  • the Brihadisvara temple of the Cholas at Thanjavur;
  • the Kandariya Mahadeva at Khajuraho;
  • Banteay Srei near Angkor in Cambodia;
  • the shrines of Mỹ Sơn in the Cham lands of Vietnam;
  • the central and tallest shrine of Prambanan in Java.
